qs.q: What is the single most common source of arterial emboli leading to focal cerebral ischemia and infarction in the middle cerebral artery territory?
qs.e: Cardiac sources, particularly mural thrombi from myocardial infarction or atrial fibrillation, are the most common origin of cerebral emboli. Fat and tumor emboli occur less frequently.

qs.q: A 72-year-old man dies following a large middle cerebral artery stroke. Histological examination of the brain tissue at day five would predominantly demonstrate which finding?
qs.e: Phagocytic cells, consisting of monocyte-derived macrophages and activated microglia, become the predominant cell type clearing tissue debris by 48 to 72 hours. Neutrophils peak earlier within the first 24 to 48 hours rather than persisting or dominating at five days.
